claim: F evaluates the supported HNN++ Poincare convolution score from sufficient statistics while preserving the implemented clipping and filter-norm floor.
scope: Supported convolution and dense score boundaries implemented by R and F under the declared FP32/FP64 projection contract.
caveat: The statement is an algebraic and implementation claim for the specified operator; it is not a claim about arbitrary hyperbolic layers or finite-precision bitwise identity.
manuscript_destination: Method: Conventions and preserved layer; Factorizing the patch computation; Numerical contract and compared variants

claim: The repaired numerical contract passes every registered smooth and N088 check and every structured F row; 33 finite T/FP32 small-U-Net rows miss the registered aggregate tolerance.
scope: The accepted 424-row bounded repair suite and 3800-row structured follow-up in the compact numerical release.
caveat: Exact-cap and clipping-kink rows are diagnostics outside the smooth gate; the accepted post-repair suite is narrower than the historical pre-repair numerical sweep.

claim: F accelerates forward and forward-plus-backward execution for all three corrected convolution anchors; block and dense-stack gains are smaller or uncertain.
scope: Five paired V100/CUDA-11.8 sessions for S1-S3 convolution anchors, Conv-BN-ReLU, and one depth-four dense stack.
caveat: There is no accepted post-repair E04 one-factor scaling sweep, broad dense grid, second GPU, or portability claim.
manuscript_destination: Results: Operator and block timing; Discussion and limitations

claim: In the controlled Poincare U-Net, F reduces batch-eight complete-update latency and process-lifetime peak live allocation relative to R.
scope: Five paired sessions for batch-one and batch-eight forward boundaries and the batch-eight complete Adam update on one 32-GB V100/CUDA-11.8 system.
caveat: The memory field is a process-lifetime JAX allocator peak; the full-model timing matrix does not include ResNet, a second platform, or a standalone backward boundary.
manuscript_destination: Results: Complete U-Net timing, memory, and profile

claim: The accepted complete-U-Net profile identifies reductions as the largest remaining cumulative device-kernel-time category after factorization.
scope: One descriptive 20-call trace of the batch-eight complete U-Net update for R, F, and T.
caveat: Cumulative kernel time can overlap and is not bounded by module span; the profile does not cover every operator anchor or the ResNet model.
manuscript_destination: Results: Complete U-Net timing, memory, and profile

claim: All fifteen ISIC16 R/F/T runs completed; F training compute is faster than R, while the fixed-final F-R Dice interval spans zero and does not establish noninferiority.
scope: Five matched seeds per variant, 5100 updates, prespecified fixed-final official-test endpoint, and secondary validation-selected endpoint.
caveat: Only five paired seeds were used, no noninferiority margin was registered, and current-batch normalization makes duplicate-excluded reevaluation sensitive to changed batch composition.
manuscript_destination: Results: Training efficiency and task outcomes; Appendix: Secondary and seed-level results

claim: All fifteen CIFAR-100 R/F/T runs completed; F training compute is faster than R, while the positive fixed-final F-R accuracy point estimate is descriptive rather than an accuracy contribution.
scope: Five matched seeds per variant, 35200 updates, prespecified fixed-final official-test endpoint, and secondary validation-selected endpoint.
caveat: The fixed-final paired interval spans zero, five pairs provide limited resolution, and the result does not imply that factorization defines a more accurate model.
manuscript_destination: Results: Training efficiency and task outcomes; Appendix: Secondary and seed-level results

claim: At fixed retained U-Net weights and identical batches, R/F/T forward outputs and selected activations agree within the reported numerical errors.
scope: All ten registered final E09 R/T source checkpoints, two evaluation partitions, and R/F/T candidate execution paths.
caveat: The registered replay did not use F-trained source checkpoints and is not an all-final-checkpoint ResNet replay; fixed-weight forward agreement does not establish equal training trajectories.
manuscript_destination: Repository-only supporting diagnostic; omitted from the concise manuscript after the author scope revision

claim: The six-source retained-state diagnostic supports small fixed-state forward discrepancies but does not support gradient- or update-level numerical interchangeability for ResNet-20.
scope: Seed-11 R/F/T trained source states for E09 and E10, each evaluated through R, F, T, repeated-R, and one-ULP control paths through 100 post-budget updates.
caveat: The six states are correlated single-seed diagnostics rather than independent task-quality replicates, and the continuation does not identify the cause of terminal quality differences.
manuscript_destination: Discussion and limitations: one bounded ResNet gradient/update sentence; full diagnostic remains repository-only

claim: The systems timing, memory, profile, and scaling evidence is limited to one V100/CUDA-11.8 platform; training evidence comprises separate original V100 and prospective A6000 cohorts for the same two convolutional task models.
scope: The current paper and compact evidence bundle after the post-repair scope amendments and the jointly gated E20/E21 export.
caveat: The unauditable pilot and historical pre-repair results are excluded; E04, broad E05/E06/E08/E11 coverage, E12, and E14 are not claimed as complete. E09/E10 and E20/E21 are not pooled, the cohort/platform change is confounded, and no causal hardware or CUDA-12 portability claim is made.
manuscript_destination: Discussion and limitations; Code and data availability

claim: Across the complete-U-Net update scaling sweep, F was faster and used less process-lifetime peak live allocation than R at every workload where both paths completed; at batch 8 and 512 x 512, all five F sessions completed while all five R sessions ended in recorded first-update allocator OOMs.
scope: Seven registered workloads spanning batch sizes 1, 2, 4, 8, and 16 at 256 x 256 and resolutions 128, 256, and 512 at batch 8; five fresh-process sessions per path on one V100 with 32 GiB physical memory under CUDA 11.8 and a captured 23.81-GiB JAX allocator limit.
caveat: The 512 x 512 speedup is not estimable because R did not complete; the failure diagnostic reports a 23.01-GiB compiled allocation under the captured allocator limit, not exhaustion of all physical memory; peak live allocation includes initialization, compilation, and warmup and is not isolated activation memory; capacity and timing are allocator-, platform-, and implementation-specific.
manuscript_destination: Results: Complete U-Net timing, memory, and scaling; Discussion and limitations

claim: All 30 registered E20 U-Net R/F runs passed the joint gate. On the A6000 cohort, the R/F speedup was 2.017 [1.992, 2.042] for synchronized update compute and 1.646 [1.610, 1.682] for whole-worker elapsed time; fixed-final F-R Dice was +0.00263 [-0.00478, 0.01004].
scope: Fifteen new matched seeds per variant, 5100 updates, protocol 1.14, prespecified fixed-final official-test endpoint, and registered secondary endpoints on one RTX A6000 using the pinned CUDA-11.8 user-space runtime.
caveat: The Dice interval spans zero and no noninferiority or equivalence margin was registered. This cohort remains separate from E09; current-batch normalization affects the duplicate-excluded sensitivity, and no causal hardware comparison is supported.
manuscript_destination: Results: Training efficiency and task outcomes; Appendix: Replication and seed-level results

claim: All 30 registered E21 ResNet-20 R/F runs passed the joint gate. On the A6000 cohort, the R/F speedup was 1.764 [1.741, 1.787] for synchronized update compute and 1.655 [1.624, 1.686] for whole-worker elapsed time; fixed-final F-R accuracy was -0.00171 [-0.00553, 0.00210].
scope: Fifteen new matched seeds per variant, 35200 updates, protocol 1.14, prespecified fixed-final official-test endpoint, and registered secondary endpoints on the same RTX A6000 and pinned CUDA-11.8 user-space runtime as E20.
caveat: The accuracy interval spans zero and no noninferiority or equivalence margin was registered. This cohort remains separate from E10; the cohort/platform change is confounded and no causal hardware comparison is supported.
manuscript_destination: Results: Training efficiency and task outcomes; Appendix: Replication and seed-level results

claim: A same-machine clean-clone technical preflight reproduced the bounded E02 acceptance gate and the direction of the batch-eight complete-U-Net update gain: 424 numerical rows with 40/40 required same-precision groups, and paired R/F speedup 1.745 [1.557, 1.956].
scope: One author-authorized, Codex-operated clean clone of release-candidate commit 93fb31a11a008ba1a378434071cb418b504092d9 on physical V100 GPU 1; five fresh-process R/F/T timing sessions, 50 warmups, and 200 synchronized observations per group.
caveat: This is same-host technical reproducibility evidence, not an independent-human reproduction or portability test. It did not rerun training, the 1360-row structured matrix, or E08 peak allocation, and its estimate is not pooled with E08.
manuscript_destination: Results: Complete U-Net timing, memory, scaling, and profile; Code and data availability
